slides.title: Welcome to the Children's Constitution Club!
slides.subtitle: KREIS × CMCA
slides.tip: Welcome music as children enter. Single centered title.

slides.title: Teacher introduces themselves
body: My name is ____
I am your Children's Constitution Club teacher
Something I like / something I don't:
slides.tip: Introduce yourself. Share one thing you like and one you don't — model openness.

slides.title: Master Change introduces himself
slides.transcript: Hello little citizens! I am Master Change. I am here to help your teacher and you. Welcome to your Children's Constitution Club! This year, as a Change Champion, I am also a member of your Club. CMCA — Children's Movement for Civic Awareness — helps children become thinking, questioning citizens who work for society. I will be with you and your teacher as a guide. Along with CMCA, there are partner organisations helping bring the Children's Constitution Club to you. Can you all clap for CMCA, the partner organisations, and me? Thank you for your warm welcome! Let's begin our journey as members of our Children's Constitution Club — the CC Club!
slides.tip: Play the full MC video.

images.caption: Navu Prathishtana · Mysuru, Kodagu, Kalaburgi, Bidar, Yadgir
Prakruthi Foundation · Tumkur, Hassan, Bangalore Urban & Rural

slides.title: One Two — Eyes on You
body: Teacher: "One, two — eyes on me!"
Children whisper: "Eyes on you."
slides.tip: Use this calmer whenever you need to settle the class.

slides.title: Let's calm down again!
body: Teacher: "Flat tyre!"
Children: "Shhhhhh!"
slides.tip: Energiser.

slides.title: Form Groups
body: Let's form groups — every voice matters.
Groups are for sharing, listening, and learning together.
slides.tip: Use a counting method to form 5–6 child mixed-gender groups.

slides.title: Let's get creative!
slides.brief: Name your group, make a group logo. For example: look at the KSRTC and KREIS logos.
slides.tip: Start 8-min timer. Soft chime when 2 min remain. After 8 min, each group shows their name + logo.

slides.title: Now let's see who's the winner
slides.tip: Watch the video. It will auto-pause after each question. Tell the class: "Quick — show of hands! 8 seconds." If the class is noisy, settle them before pressing Skip.
slides.transcript: Master Change asks 7 group-reflection questions: (1) Did everyone share their thoughts about the name or logo? (2) Was it easy to choose one name or logo? (3) How did you decide which idea to pick? (4) Did everyone get a chance to share their opinion? (5) Did everyone get a chance to draw at least part of the logo? (6) Did you feel your idea was heard and respected? (7) When you showed your image, did everyone come together to display it?

slides.title: Think & Share
slides.prompt: From this group activity of naming your group and making a logo — what did you learn?
slides.tip: Get answers from 3–4 children.
slides.callout: ✍ Smartboard — write children's answers on the board

slides.title: Master Change wraps the activity
slides.transcript: You have now practiced something very important. When you listen to each other, share your ideas, and work together, you become true Constitution Champions. From now on, make sure everyone takes part in group activities. From the start of every Club session, sit together with your group. Now it's time for the Constitution Connect Question!
slides.tip: Play the video.

slides.title: Constitution Connect Question
slides.scenario: You are doing a school team project with 8 classmates. The Preamble's words 'We the People' show how important it is to work together. How does this fit your project?
options: Try to convince all members that your decision is the best.
Without understanding, accept others' decisions just to please them.
Think keeping all members' wellbeing in mind.
Argue among yourselves and work separately.
slides.tip: Read the scenario aloud. Give children time to guess before revealing. Correct answer: c) Think keeping all members' wellbeing in mind.

slides.title: Constitution Connect Question
slides.tip: Read each line calmly. This is the reflective beat of the session.
body: Good effort!
The Preamble words "We, the People of India" remind us that government is built by the people, for the people.
When your group takes decisions, remember every member — that is what the Constitution asks of us.
From every session onwards, a Constitution Connect Question will follow — a small link back to what the Constitution says.
Now let's move on to the next activity!

slides.title: Make rules together — Think & Share
slides.intro: While you answer these 2 questions, your teacher listens with you.
prompts: Imagine you're about to play a really fun new game. What do you need to know to play it properly?
If everyone starts playing as they like, and doesn't listen to the umpire/referee/judge, what happens to the game?
slides.tip: Show one question at a time. Get 1–2 answers per question before moving on.

slides.title: What is Master Change doing?
slides.intro_text: Time to make Club rules. Let's see an example. What is Master Change doing here?
post_video_text: Raising his hand to speak. As a child — this is YOUR rule.
As a teacher — trying to give everyone a chance to speak — this is MY rule.
slides.tip: Loop animation while children watch. Press NEXT/REVEAL when ready.

slides.title: Write rules in your group
slides.brief: Using paper/post-its, write 1 rule for yourself and 1 rule for your teacher to follow.
slides.tip: Distribute paper before starting timer. 3-min timer.

slides.title: Present the rules
body: Each group shares one rule — no repeats!
slides.tip: Go group by group. If a rule is already taken, that group shares a different one.

slides.title: Think & Share
slides.prompt: What should we do if someone doesn't follow the rules?
slides.tip: 2–3 children's answers.

slides.title: More rules for the Club to succeed
slides.callout: Teachers, please add the rule: "Treat everyone with respect."
slides.tip: Play through.
body: There are seven rules for the Club to succeed: ONE — first, be the change you want to see
TWO — share your opinion without fear
THREE — cooperate and respect time
FOUR — everyone is important
FIVE — keep your mind open to new ideas
SIX — share your experiences
SEVEN — working as a team is always better and more fun
Teachers, please add one more: treat everyone with respect

slides.title: Who inspires us?
body: Just as our Club has rules, our country has a whole book of rules — and so much more!
Clue: who inspires us as citizens of India?
slides.tip: Ask for a few guesses.

slides.title: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and the Constituent Assembly
slides.transcript: We draw inspiration from the vision our Constitution holds for India — it guides us and motivates us. In honour of the Constitution, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, and the members of the Constituent Assembly, we will end this session of the Constitution Club's learning journey by all of us together reading the Preamble.
slides.tip: Play the video. Pause for guesses on who inspires us.

slides.title: Constitution Connect Question
slides.scenario: Why does our school have a Children's Constitution Club?
options: To learn about rights, responsibilities, and democracy
slides.tip: Read aloud. Give children time to guess. Click to reveal.

slides.title: Constitution Connect Question
slides.scenario: What is a campaign in the Children's Constitution Club?
options: A way to raise awareness about a problem and bring change
slides.tip: Read aloud. Give children time to guess. Click to reveal.

slides.title: Constitution Connect Question
slides.scenario: Which is a key value in the Children's Constitution Club?
slides.tip: Read aloud. Give children time to guess. Click to reveal.

slides.title: Ripples of Change
body: Now let's talk about Ripples of Change — how one small action can lead to a big impact.
Asfiya, a member of the Children's Constitution Club, is a clear example.
Her small efforts brought positive change at her school, in her town, and beyond.
slides.tip: Tell the children: even one small effort can become a 'ripple of change.' Asfiya's story is next — about 3 minutes.

slides.title: Asfiya's Story
slides.tip: Play uninterrupted. After it ends, get children's reactions.
slides.transcript: Asfiya was a member of the Children's Constitution Club. While studying in 8th grade, she and her friends brought a positive change at school by replacing paper cups with steel tumblers. Beyond school, in her community, she responded to civic problems — helping injured animals, planting trees, and supporting those in need. Even when some people discouraged her, she continued her efforts to do good for society. Today, she remains active in service work and dreams of becoming a doctor to help even more people. Asfiya's story shows us that even small efforts can lead to big change. 🌱

slides.title: Let's read the Preamble of India together
slides.tip: Stand up. Read together. Slowly, clearly.

slides.title: Children's Constitution Club
slides.closing_line: Today our Constitution Club journey has had a great start. See you again in the next session.
slides.tip: Thank the children. End of session.
